opportunities.name: GitHub candidate lead → hiring email
opportunities.description: Look up a GitHub user's profile and top repo, then draft a lead email to hiring@example.com for role {role} summarizing {username}'s followers, top repo, stars, language and latest post.
steps: On GitHub, open the 'Search or jump to' box
Clear it and type {username}, press Enter
Click the 'Users' results filter
Click the {username} user result
Note follower count and latest blog post; open the top/pinned repo and note stars and language
In mail, click 'To' and type hiring@example.com
Set Subject to 'Lead for {role}: {username}'
Set Body to '{username}: {followers} followers, top repo {repo} ({stars} stars, {language}), latest post: {latest_post}.'
Send/close the draft

instances.values: username=karpathy, role=ML Research Engineer, repo=nanoGPT (63.8k, Python), 226k followers
username=gaearon, role=Staff Frontend Engineer, repo=react/react (251.1k, JavaScript), 94k followers
username=simonw, role=Developer Advocate, repo=llm (12.6k, Python), 17.3k followers (interrupted by Chicago Loop lookup)

opportunities.name: Person bio + Wayback homepage snapshot → note
opportunities.description: Look up {person} on Wikipedia for birth date and role, then view {domain} in the Wayback Machine for {year} and record the headline in a new note.
steps: On Wikipedia, click the search box, select all, type {person}, press Enter
Dismiss any banner and note birth date and current role
On the Wayback Machine, type {domain} into the URL box and press Enter
Click year {year} in the timeline
Click a capture day in the calendar to open the snapshot
Read the main headline on the archived homepage
In notes, click 'New note' and type '{person}: born {birth_date}, {role}. {domain} in {year}: {headline}', press Enter

opportunities.name: Address nearest park (OpenStreetMap) + neighborhood summary → note
opportunities.description: For {address}, find the nearest park, distance and walking time on OpenStreetMap, look up {neighborhood} on Wikipedia, and record both in a note (OSM kept returning HTTP 429).
steps: Open OpenStreetMap and search for {address} (reload if rate-limited)
Find the nearest park and get walking directions for distance and time
On Wikipedia, search {neighborhood} and read the summary
In notes, add '{address}: nearest park {park}, distance {distance}, walking time {time}. {neighborhood}: {summary}'

instances.values: address=233 S Wacker Dr, Chicago; neighborhood=Chicago Loop; park unavailable (429)
